statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds in the high band on a ten-year Treasury yield near its highest since 2007, market pricing of roughly a 70% chance of another Fed hike in October, WTI at $92.41 with the Strait of Hormuz closed for a 211th day, and Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day reopening roadmap.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures still shut in the final hour before the 22:00Z restart, while a ten-year yield near 2007 highs, October hike pricing near 70% and an unresolved Hormuz closure hold Stress high
body: This assessment falls in the last full hour before the 22:00Z Globex restart. CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path and the low current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash session was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,608.14, up 129.23 points or 0.42% from a 30,478.90 prior close and inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 within a 14.68-15.94 range. The NQ December 2026 contract last traded 30,889.25, up 0.40%, on 25 September. Breadth was firm but dispersed: Microsoft rose 3.7% on Copilot product consolidation plans while Meta fell 3.3%, and hardware names led with Applied Materials up 2.3% and Lam Research up 2.6%. The bond backdrop is the dominant Stress input and hardened further this week. The ten-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 during the week, rising about 23 basis points over three sessions to around 5.20% before easing to roughly 5.17% at Friday's close; the H.15 release dated 25 September shows 4.87% at two years, 5.18% at ten years and 5.47% at thirty years for 24 September values, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% after the FOMC's 25 basis point increase on 16 September. The thirty-year sits near 5.50%, close to 2004 highs, and markets now price roughly a 66-70% probability of a further 25 basis point hike at the 27-28 October meeting, with the September University of Michigan survey having shown a sharp rise in inflation expectations. Equities absorbed that backdrop rather than breaking under it, which is precisely why Stress is high while Tail is low. Geopolitics hardened over the weekend. Trump rejected Iran's phased proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the seventh day, calling the terms unacceptable, and Iran's conditions of lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions, releasing frozen funds and observing a regional ceasefire remain in place with Foreign Minister Araghchi awaiting a definitive response through mediators. The IRGC Navy claimed it seized a second U.S. Remus 600 underwater vehicle in the strait; CENTCOM denied the account and said it retains positive control of all operational drone assets. Iranian media reported two explosions heard off Qeshm Island on 26 September hours after the rejection, but Iranian authorities did not confirm any attack that day, so that report is treated as unverified and does not move Tail. The strait is now in a 211th day of effective closure, with one recorded transit on 20 September against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 per day and about 174 vessels holding position in the area, while the U.S. Energy Secretary reports a running crude transit average near 13 million barrels per day via alternative escorted routes. The material market consequence is unchanged and narrow: part of Friday's 2.33% WTI decline to $92.41 and the parallel 2.14% Brent decline to $104.32 rested on a diplomatic premise that has since been explicitly withdrawn, and neither oil nor equity futures have traded since. That creates a genuine reopening-gap and two-way-discovery mechanism at 22:00Z rather than evidence of a formed one-way path, which is why the danger window is confined to the restart and early Asian hours instead of being widened across Monday. Shared Finviz context was read and is both stale at roughly three hours and partial, with its calendar and futures sections unavailable; its usable latest-session breadth independently matched Friday's verified cash tone, with Technology up 0.85%, six of eight megacaps higher at wide dispersion and six of seven tracked semiconductors higher. That tone is delayed, non-real-time context with no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure, so it informs Stress and Confidence only. Stress is held in the high band on the yield and rate-expectations backdrop, the unresolved strait closure, the withdrawn diplomacy and a catalyst stack running through Wednesday's core PCE, quarter-end and Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close, Thursday's ISM and Friday's payrolls. Confidence is high because current index, volatility, yield, rate-expectation, oil, shipping and calendar levels were verified directly from primary and reputable sources this run, and is held below the very-high band by the single unavoidable gap: no live price path exists until the restart.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged without hindsight revision. Tail held in a narrow 6-10 band, Stress rose from 54 to 73 with a shallow overnight dip to 52, and Confidence decayed from 77 to a 67 trough around 08:00Z before recovering to 78 by 20:00Z. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a closed-futures weekend in which risk accumulated through headlines and the bond market rather than through an observed price path.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk peaks inside the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz roadmap, Tehran's refusal to soften its terms and Friday's now-unsupported oil decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. From the early Asian hours the path steps back down on the assumption that reopening imbalance is absorbed with visible retracements, then rises again modestly into Monday's 13:30Z U.S. cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed print, which are checkpoints rather than structural Tail drivers, once more around the 17:30Z Barkin remarks given October hike pricing near 70%, and again into the 19:00Z power hour on quarter-end rebalancing. Every elevated forecast hour is conditional gap, liquidity-transition or flow risk; none asserts that one-way structure has already been observed. Stress stays high throughout on a ten-year yield near 2007 highs and an unresolved strait closure, and Wednesday's core PCE, quarter-end and Micron results, Thursday's ISM and Friday's payrolls dominate the wider week.
